scope: All 28 baseline public no-coverage models; complete current 117-career catalog scanned. Five recovered exploration scenarios, not validated matches or guaranteed outcomes.
methods: Review current interests, recent biography, field preferences and career-specific answers for every baseline case.
Independently calculate first-paid-stage lifestyle budgets across all 117 current careers, excluding roles requiring prior experience.
Compare higher-pay alternatives with actual interest evidence; do not treat a correlation or salary alone as a justified choice.

Repair only two exclusion paths: use the supported Top matches displayed on the page as related-search seeds; retain strongly evidenced task-related options despite incomplete broad field confirmation.

Task-related options require completed field follow-ups, at least six distinct selected question groups, three refinements, four focused answers, two task domains, positive destination-field evidence, correlation at least 0.20, and no route/clinical/field conflict. Flat profiles remain open.
Keep core scores, official answers, Top matches, pay references and budget assumptions unchanged.

rows.name: Mateo Quintero
rows.evidence: Bicycle diagnosis, fabrication, bench work and eight mechanical-repair choices.
rows.judgment: Repair and machinery roles fit; their starting pay does not meet the $75K target. An engineer title would require design/calculation interests that are not established by liking repairs.
rows.next: Try machine-maintenance or fabrication work; compare the lifestyle with actual starting repair wages.

rows.name: Cora McIntyre
rows.evidence: Essays, library discussion, reliable sources and eight library/resource choices.
rows.judgment: Library and community-research work deserve exploration and are now retained as related task options, but their starting pay is below $75K. A high speech-pathology correlation does not establish interest in clinical communication assessment.
rows.next: Try resource-finding or community research; separately ask about data-analysis or clinical work before offering it as a match.

rows.name: Evelyn Duarte
rows.evidence: Coordinates study groups, changing event plans and deadlines; eight project-planning choices.
rows.judgment: Project coordination is coherent, but the $85K goal exceeds its starting reference. Operations, consulting and healthcare management require earlier experience; therapy careers cannot be substituted merely for higher pay.
rows.next: Compare a project-support introduction and entry pay; keep later management separate from the first job.

rows.name: Miles Pruett
rows.evidence: Setup instructions, supply locations, painting surfaces and eight facilities/checklist choices.
rows.judgment: Facilities and maintenance work fit the stated tasks and are now retained as related options, but do not support a $75K starting budget. Coding is unfamiliar; its profile correlation is insufficient to make it a career choice.
rows.next: Try a facilities project and tools introduction; do not equate a calm or undecided profile with engineering or software interest.

rows.name: Marisol Treviño
rows.evidence: Ceramic products, glazing, measuring and eight useful-object design choices.
rows.judgment: Industrial design is the right direction to explore. Its roughly $65K displayed entry reference falls short of a $70K target. Higher-paying clinical work is not supported by the recorded tasks.
rows.next: Compare the modest budget gap and training costs without inventing a higher starting wage.

rows.name: Aisha Ellery
rows.evidence: Repeatable robotics tests, failed-trial records, data quality and uncertainty; eight analysis choices.
rows.judgment: Data science and statistics were missing because a broad software/device question did not confirm the whole technology field. Repeated analysis-specific answers justify related options. Both pass the existing budget; statistics has little monthly room.
rows.next: Try a public-data analysis and inspect the required mathematics/programming study. Clinical roles remain unconfirmed despite high profile correlations.

rows.name: Rhett Calder
rows.evidence: Recorded rural stories, dialogue revision, audio editing and eight story-production choices.
rows.judgment: Writing, editing and animation are sensible; their entry references do not meet $75K. Higher-paid therapy is not supported by this storytelling history.
rows.next: Explore editing/storytelling; investigate technical communication separately if explaining products or processes is appealing.

rows.name: Hodan Farah
rows.evidence: Scheduled peer tutoring, several ways to explain fractions and older-student teaching choices.
rows.judgment: Subject teaching fits, but the local starting teacher reference is below $65K. Enjoying explanations does not establish interest in hands-on clinical treatment.
rows.next: Inspect teacher work and the budget. Adult training is a catalog follow-up, with its experience requirements kept explicit.

rows.name: Greta Halvorsen
rows.evidence: Service supplies, clear labels, concrete visitor questions and eight office-coordination choices.
rows.judgment: Administrative and office work are coherent, but their starting pay does not meet $60K. High health-care correlations do not establish patient-care interest.
rows.next: Explore inventory/purchasing duties and supplier negotiation before adding a purchasing option; verify its own Austin entry wage.

rows.name: Evan Rourke
rows.evidence: Documentary sequencing, audio stories and eight moving-image/story choices.
rows.judgment: Film editing, writing and animation fit; their starting references remain below $70K. Robotics participation alone does not justify a higher-paying software or engineering role.
rows.next: Try sustained editing or a technical-explanation project; preserve learning supports rather than using them to exclude occupations.

rows.name: Julian Adebayo
rows.evidence: Sustained poetry revision, careful word choices, audience engagement and eight narrative choices.
rows.judgment: Writing is better supported than operating a business or building software. Its entry pay is below $70K. An app pitch or confidence claim does not establish software or management interest.
rows.next: Continue audience-focused writing; ask about technical subjects before treating technical writing as a fit.

rows.name: Caleb Whitlock
rows.evidence: One-off wood projects, careful sanding, scenery and seven woodworking choices.
rows.judgment: Carpentry/custom fabrication fit, but starting pay is below $75K. Producing unique objects does not establish interest in medical rehabilitation or engineering calculations.
rows.next: Explore woodworking or scenery/exhibit fabrication; keep production repetition and actual starting pay visible.

rows.name: Nadia Flores
rows.evidence: Fact checking, documents, neighborhood-history interviews and eight information-resource choices.
rows.judgment: Library/community-information work is justified and is now retained as a related option, but the library entry reference is below $60K. A clinical career requires new task evidence.
rows.next: Try public-history/resource work and ask whether explaining technical processes is appealing.

rows.name: Zara Hassan
rows.evidence: Colors, readable labels, story meaning, poster revision and repeated visual-communication choices.
rows.judgment: Writing and graphic design were being suppressed by the broad field gate and are now available as related task options, but their starting wages are below $60K. Website/interface work is a useful follow-up question, not an automatic fit from color preference.
rows.next: Try a manageable poster or interface-usability exercise and collect the new preference before claiming a digital-design match.

rows.name: Rafael Yazzie
rows.evidence: Audio interviews, environmental storytelling, editing and accurate representation.
rows.judgment: Media and language options fit and are retained more fully after the task-evidence repair. Their entry wages remain below $65K. Geoscience or interface design needs evidence of those different daily tasks.
rows.next: Try a completed environmental-media piece; distinguish liking a landscape from wanting geological analysis.

rows.name: Linh Cabrera
rows.evidence: Color experiments, drawing, visual storytelling and seven animation-linked follow-up choices.
rows.judgment: Animation was incorrectly lost when broad creative-field confirmation was incomplete. It is now a related option and narrowly covers the $60K target under the unchanged budget. That is an exploration scenario, not a job guarantee.
rows.next: Try an animation/storyboard project and examine required digital tools, portfolio preparation and income variability.

rows.name: Nolan Ashford
rows.evidence: Cooking a complete weekly meal, shared supplies and eight food-preparation choices; broader preferences remain weak.
rows.judgment: Food preparation is a reasonable introductory activity, but $60K starting pay is not supported. Higher-paid imaging or software careers are not justified by the current biography alone.
rows.next: Repeat a real food-service experience and review preferences; do not turn unfamiliar high-paying activities into matches.

rows.name: Zoe Min Park
rows.evidence: Cake decoration, recipe scaling, welcoming events and repeated food/service choices.
rows.judgment: Food and hospitality fit. Their starting pay does not meet $65K, and restaurant management requires experience. Visual/interface work is a possible new trial, but cake decoration is not evidence of interface-design duties.
rows.next: Try a small visual-design/usability project if desired, then collect occupation-specific answers.

rows.name: Wyatt Sloane
rows.evidence: Repeated baking methods, detailed sequences, supply sorting and eight food-preparation choices.
rows.judgment: Food preparation fits; $60K entry pay does not. Industrial engineering, food science and diagnostic imaging need new evidence of their technical daily work rather than recipe-following alone.
rows.next: Sample production-quality or food-lab work if curious; keep chef/management advancement distinct from entry.

rows.name: Imani Westbrook
rows.evidence: Oral histories, exhibit captions, audience-focused narratives, film/story choices and two positive creative-field responses.
rows.judgment: Film editing was shown in Top matches but absent from the related-search seeds. Restoring it surfaces affordable website/interface and product-design ideas under the existing related-career rules. These are cross-specialty trials; physical-product design has little direct task evidence and must not be presented as a confirmed fit.
rows.next: Prioritize a content/usability exercise; use a separate prototype trial before treating physical-product design as a preference.

rows.name: Gabriel Soto-Ruiz
rows.evidence: Adapts activities to children, notices learning needs and repeatedly chooses teaching tasks.
rows.judgment: A tie left the old engine list empty even though the new page displayed three teaching matches. Related search now uses those displayed careers, recovering occupational therapy and school psychology. They require different clinical/assessment study and are exploration options, not automatic teaching promotions.
rows.next: Ask about clinical rehabilitation versus psychological assessment and show the full qualification route before any career choice.

rows.name: Noah Feld
rows.evidence: Stock counts, duplicate entries, financial records and repeated accounting/financial-analysis choices; explicitly dislikes clinical discussions.
rows.judgment: Records and finance fit, but accounting and financial-analysis entry references do not meet $80K. Software or law should not be added merely to close the gap without role-specific evidence.
rows.next: Explore purchasing/inventory analysis as a catalog gap, with supplier negotiation, training and local entry pay checked first.

rows.name: Audrey Whitfield
rows.evidence: Invitations, appointment coordination, product comparisons and seven office/sales task choices; broad academic preferences are tentative.
rows.judgment: The displayed administrative-assistant match was missing from the related-search seeds. Including it recovers project coordination, human resources and logistics with entry scenarios that cover $50K. Her career preference remains tentative; these are related ideas requiring real task trials, not evidence that polished presentations imply readiness.
rows.next: Try scheduling, an HR-support task or a materials-flow exercise and revisit interest. HR has little monthly budget room.

rows.name: Lee
rows.evidence: Diagnostic reasoning interests conflict with a shorter dental-assisting route; the lifestyle target is $320K.
rows.judgment: No catalog first-paid-stage scenario supports this budget. Physician responsibility also conflicts with the selected assisting route. Neither high-pay specialization nor residency can be substituted for a realistic starting salary.
rows.next: Resolve the responsibility/training preference and compare a realistic first-work-stage budget.

rows.name: River
rows.evidence: Bridge failure notes, load calculations, safety constraints and eight civil-engineering choices.
rows.judgment: Civil engineering is strongly justified. The $120K target reflects starter-home ownership, a financed used car and $1,500 monthly saving; it is not just the cost of modest consumption. Engineering entry pay falls short. Dentistry cannot be substituted on pay alone.
rows.next: Review the timing of home ownership and saving as scenarios without overwriting the recorded preferences.

rows.name: Sky
rows.evidence: Recipe tests and cooking sequence, explicitly excluding supervision, bargaining and ownership.
rows.judgment: Cook/food-preparation interests are real, but $46K at entry is not supported by the current references. Chef or restaurant-management pay cannot stand in for a first kitchen job or her preferred duties.
rows.next: Observe a training kitchen and actual entry schedules; do not steer toward clinical work solely because the six-score correlation is high.

rows.name: Remy
rows.evidence: Equal RIASEC totals, no selected follow-up tasks and explicit uncertainty about unfamiliar work.
rows.judgment: No differentiated interest match is justified yet. The $44K goal is not the reason for the empty result: many catalog salaries could cover it, but there is no basis to pick one for this model.
rows.next: Offer supported introductions, then revisit preferences. Do not fabricate a specialist interest.

rows.name: Charlie
rows.evidence: Equal high totals, broad enthusiastic selections and little sustained comparative experience.
rows.judgment: No differentiated match is justified. The $49K goal is not an excessive expectation; selecting an affordable occupation from many enthusiastic yeses would create false precision.
rows.next: Repeat contrasting work samples and compare what remains enjoyable after novelty fades.
